STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.claim: The surah opens by describing the virtues and righteous actions of believers.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r2.anchor: begins by describing the virtues and righteous actions of those who believe

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r2.claim: Zakāh is the second pillar and, though its legal form varied across religions, broadly means spending for God's cause; in this Makkan sūrah it means charity, not purification as a verbal noun.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r2.anchor: here it is not used as term; it refers to charity in general. Those have interpreted it in the connotation of a verbal noun to mean “purification” are mistaken.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r3.claim: Prayer joins a person to God and zakāh to fellow people; together they make one rightly connected to Creator and community worthy of success in both worlds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r3.anchor: The prayer joins a person with God and zakāh joins him to his brethren.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r4.claim: Prayer and zakāh are two arms of faith grounded in gratitude: gratitude moves believers to pray, spend, and sacrifice, so zakāh manifests and complements prayer and each necessitates the other.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r4.anchor: the common thing between both is gratitude to God. It is this sense of gratitude that urges a believer to the prayer

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r5.claim: The earlier point about humble, fearful prayer preventing sin leads into the additional benefits of prayer discussed next.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p240/r5.anchor: the essence of the prayer is also humility and fear, as mentioned earlier. In this capacity, it stops a person from every sin and vulgarity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.claim: Al-Mu'minūn's opening describes success through humble prayer, avoiding frivolity, zakāh, chastity and restraint, trustworthiness, and keeping promises.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p287/r2.anchor: salvation and success before God is reserved for those believers whose prayers are marked with humility and concentration

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r4.claim: When an active participle's object precedes it, the lām may strengthen its transitivity as with a verb; the same is possible after it, though fronting is commoner, and accusative would also be Arabic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r4.anchor: إذا تقدم معمول اسم الفاعل جاز أن يقوى تعديته باللام كالفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r5.claim: If zakāh means purification, the action can be attributed to it; if it means the payment, the phrase elides its performance or uses fāʿilūn to mean those who deliver it, as al-Tabrīzī explains.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r5.anchor: وإن أريد بالزكاة قدر ما يخرج من المال للفقير فيكون على حذف أي لأداء الزكاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r6.claim: Zakah here can mean righteous action, as in the phrase describing something better in zakāh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r6.anchor: وقيل للزكاة للعمل الصالح كقوله خيرا منه زكاة أي عملا صالحا قاله أبو مسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r7.claim: Zakah can mean growth and increase; the lām is causal, with the implied sense that they do good to obtain increase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r7.anchor: وقيل: الزكاة هنا النماء والزيادة، واللام لام العلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r8.claim: Some hold that wealth is not called zakāh until it reaches the poor recipient.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r8.anchor: وقيل: المصروف لا يسمى زكاة حتى يحصل بيد الفقير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r9.claim: Some say the paid object itself is not called zakāh, making the verbal form more apt; the author rejects a foreign skeptic's demand for مؤدون as unsupported by reason or transmission and defends the Qur'an's eloquent Arabic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r9.anchor: رد على بعض زنادقة الأعاجم الأجانب عن ذوق العربية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r10.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r10.claim: The poet's plural الزكوات is cited as sound Arabic evidence for the expression; Arab eloquence scholars accepted and cited it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī prefers reading the poem's plural as referring to the paid amounts, with an omitted word for their performance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p547/r11.anchor: وحمل البيت على هذا أصح لأنها فيه مجموعة يعني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p548/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p548/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p548/r1.claim: The author rejects the preceding argument that zakāh must mean the paid object because verbal nouns cannot be pluralized: plural verbal nouns exist, and zakāh varies by type of payment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p548/r1.anchor: لم تجمع لأن التزكية مصدر، والمصادر لا تجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p548/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p548/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p548/r2.claim: The author rejects the claim that verbal nouns cannot be plural: plural examples exist, and zakāh can vary with the kind of money or produce being paid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p548/r2.anchor: وهذا غير مسلم بل قد جاء منها مجموعا ألفاظ كالعلوم والحلوم والأشغال

SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r1.claim: The lām is an added marker on the object because it precedes its governing verb and is a derived noun.
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r1.anchor: اللام مزيدة في المفعول لتقدمه على عامله ولكونه فرعا.

SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r2.claim: Zakat is originally a verbal noun and also denotes the amount taken from taxable property.
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r2.anchor: والزكاة في الأصل مصدر، ويطلق على القدر المخرج من الأعيان.

SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says zakat can name either the paid amount or the act of giving it; here the intended sense is the act, which its performers can do.
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " اسم مشترك بين عين ومعنى، فالعين: القدر الذي يخرجه المزكي من النصاب، والمعنى: فعل المزكي،

SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues that فاعلون properly attaches to the verbal noun, since an agent is said to perform the act, as in performing a blow or killing.
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r4.anchor: لأنه ما من مصدر إلا يعبر عنه بالفعل. ويقال لمحدثه فاعل. تقول للضارب: فاعل الضرب،

SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows zakat to mean the amount paid, with an omitted word الأداء; he reads Umayya's plural poem this way because the source noun is not pluralized.
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " اسم مشترك بين عين ومعنى،

SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r6.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r6.claim: Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's line uses the plural الزكوات; al-Zamakhshari takes it as referring to amounts of zakat rather than the verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r6.anchor: وقد أنشدوا لأمية بن أبي الصلت

SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r7.claim: The author explains that al-Zamakhshari answers those who thought the concrete sense impossible with فاعلون: it is not impossible by grammar, but people do not produce the zakat amounts.
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r7.anchor: قلت: إنما أحوج أبا القاسم إلى هذا أن بعضهم زعم أنه يتعين أن تكون الزكاة هنا المصدر؛

SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r8.claim: The Shaykh objects that zakat may still be a verbal noun here and pluralized because its kinds differ.
SAMIN-DURR:23:4/r8.anchor: وناقشه الشيخ فقال: " يجوز أن مصدرا وإنما جمع لاختلاف أنواعه ".

ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r1.claim: فاعلون means those who give zakat.
ZAJJAJ:v4p6/r1.anchor: وقوله: (والذين هم للزكاة فاعلون (4) معنى (فاعلون) مؤتون.

ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.claim: Believers attain a happy state through humility in prayer and active pursuit of inner purity.
ASAD-NOTES:23:1/r1.anchor: TRULY, to a happy state shall attain the believe rs: (23:2) those who humble themselves

ASAD-NOTES:23:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:1#n1/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:23:1#n1/r1.claim: Zakah here means working for or actively promoting inner purity, an interpretation also advanced by Abu Muslim.
ASAD-NOTES:23:1#n1/r1.anchor: which is the meaning of zakah in this context (Zamakhshari; the same interpretation has been advanced by Abu Muslim)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r1.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r1.claim: The apparent reading takes zakāh as purification; describing them as doing purification indirectly entails paying the due, a more eloquent metonymy and reason for this wording.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r1.anchor: وجاء في (روح المعاني) : "الظاهر أن المراد بالزكاة المعنى المصدري - أعني التزكية -

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r2.speaker: التبريزي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r2.claim: For zakāh as the due amount, one can supply an omitted word for its payment or take فاعلون to mean مؤدون; al-Tabrīzī takes the latter, though it is criticized as nonidiomatic.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r2.anchor: أو تضمن (فاعلون) معنى (مؤدون) وبذلك فسره التبريزي إلا أنه تُعُقِّب بأنه لا يقال: (فعلت الزكاة) ، أي: أديتها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r3.speaker: فتح القدير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r3.claim: Fatḥ al-Qadīr explains فعل الزكاة as paying it, using فعل because payment is an act; zakāh is a verbal noun, with the due amount also possible by supplying an omitted noun.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r3.anchor: وجاء في (فتح القدير) : "ومعنى فعلهم للزكاة تأديتهم لها فعبَّر عن التأدية بالفعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r4.claim: Zakah may mean good works and self-purification, with the emphatic lām on the object implying that they do only such good works.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r4.anchor: ويصح أن تكون الزكاة بمعنى العمل الصالح وتطهير النفس، فيحتمل أن تكون اللام زائدة مقوية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r5.claim: Alternatively, the lām marks purpose and an omitted object leaves the verb general for deeds that lead to good and purification.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p140/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون اللام لام التعليل، أي: يفعلون من أجل الزكاة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p127/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p127/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p127/r2.claim: Al-Muʾminūn says believers perform zakāh; al-Maʿārij instead describes a known share of wealth for the beggar and deprived.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p127/r2.anchor: 3- وقال في سورة المؤمنون: {والذين هُمْ لِلزَّكَاةِ فَاعِلُونَ} . وقال في سورة المعارج: {والذين في أموالهم حَقٌّ مَّعْلُومٌ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p137/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p137/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p137/r3.claim: The wording lillzakāti fāʿilūn gathers several intended meanings that alternatives would not express in the same way.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p137/r3.anchor: إن هذا التعبير يجمع معاني عدة كلها مرادة لا تُؤَدَّى في أي تعبيرٍ آخر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p137/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p137/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p137/r4.claim: Changing the emphatic lām or moving فاعلون before الزكاة alters the layered force of the construction.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p137/r4.anchor: فإنه لو حذف اللام من (الزكاة) لكونها زائدة مقوية، كما ذهب بعضهم، أو قدم (فاعلون) على (الزكاة) فحذف اللام أو أبقاها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r4.claim: The al-Muʾminūn wording is broader: zakāh includes financial worship across eight recipient classes and purification of the self, beyond the specified share for the asker and deprived in al-Maʿārij.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p166/r4.anchor: وما في سورة (المؤمنون) أعمُّ وأشملُ إذ الزكاة تشمل العبادة المالية كما تشمل طهارة النفس فهي أعلى مما في المعارج وأكمل

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r1.claim: The apparent sense of zakāt is the verbal noun tazkiya, since an action applies to the process; if it means the payment itself, an implied word for performing it is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بالزكاة المعنى المصدري أعني التزكية لأنه الذي يتعلق به فعلهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r2.speaker: التبريزي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r2.claim: Al-Tabrīzī explains the phrase as performing the payment of zakāt, either by supplying أداء or taking فاعلون to mean payers; the latter is criticized because Arabic does not idiomatically say فعلت الزكاة for paying it.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r2.anchor: وبذلك فسره التبريزي إلا أنه تعقب بأنه لا يقال فعلت الزكاة أي أديتها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r3.claim: If zakāt means purification, describing them as doing tazkiya entails the actual payment by metonymy, a more eloquent way to express it and one reason for this wording over والذين يزكون.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r3.anchor: وإذا أريد المعنى الأول ادى وصفهم بفعل التزكية إلى أداء العين بطريق الكناية التي هي أبلغ

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r4.claim: Several earlier explanations for the greater eloquence of turning away from idle talk rather than merely not engaging in it also apply here; the fronted object may focus information rather than restrict meaning, or imply contrast with improper spending.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r4.anchor: وجميع ما مر آنفا بيان أبلغية ( والذين هم عن اللغو معرضون ) من الذين لا يلهون جار هنا سوى الوجه الخامس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r5.claim: Positioning zakāt after prayer depicts full effort in bodily and financial worship; placing avoidance of idle talk between them links closely to prayer, though the Qurʾān often mentions the two duties together.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5/r5.anchor: ووصفهم بذلك بعد وصفهم بالخشوع في الصلاة للدلالة على أنهم لم يألوا جهدا بالعبادة والمالية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r1.claim: Abū Muslim takes zakāt here to mean righteous action, as in the phrase خيرا منه زكاة.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r1.anchor: وعن أبي مسلم أن الزكاة هنا بمعنى العمل الصالح كما في قوله تعالى ( خيرا منه زكاة )

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r2.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib chooses the sense purity, with the lām expressing purpose: they perform worship so God may purify them or they may purify themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r2.anchor: واختار الراغب أن الزكاة بمعنى الطهارة واللام للعليل والمعنى والذين يفعلون من العبادة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭībī relays al-Kashf's reading that they do good for purification of the soul, supported by verses where the Qurʾān says the one who purifies succeeds; the Qurʾān interprets itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r3.anchor: نقل نحوه الطيبي عن صاحب الكشف فقال : قال صاحب الكشف : معنى الآية الذين هم لأجل الطهارة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r4.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r4.claim: An eminent scholar argues that pairing this trait with prayer signals the financial worship of paying zakāt; the comparison to the purification verses is remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعض الأجلة : إن اقتران ذلك بالصلاة ينادي على أن المراد وصفهم بأداء الزكاة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r5.claim: A further argument for al-Rāghib's non-legal reading is that the sūra is Meccan while zakāt became obligatory in Medina, avoiding the need for earlier interpretive adjustments.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r5.anchor: وربما يقال : الفصل بينهما يشعر بما اختاره الراغب ومن حذا حذوه وأيضا كون السورة مكية والزكاة فرضت بالمدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī ridicules a non-Arab critic's claim that مؤدون would be better than فاعلون, arguing that the Prophet's eloquence was unmatched and hostile Arab critics would have seized on any real flaw.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r6.anchor: وقول بعض زنادقة الأعاجم الذين حرموا ذوق العربية : ألا قيل مؤدون بدل ( فاعلون ) من محض الجهل

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r7.claim: Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt used a similar expression, المطعمون الطعام في السنة الأزمة والفاعلون للزكوات, without objection from Arab eloquent critics, supporting the Qurʾānic diction.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r7.anchor: وقد جاء نظير ذلك في كلام أمية بن أبي الصلت قال : المطعمون الطعام في السنة الأزمة والفاعلون للزكوات

ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes zakāt as the payable amount and supplies an omitted noun; Al-Ālūsī objects that verbal nouns can also be plural and that differing objects justify pluralization here.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p5#2/r8.anchor: واختار الزمخشري في هذا حمل الزكاة على العين وتقدير المضاف دون الآية وعلل بجمعها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p409#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p409#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p409#2/r5.claim: The phrase means that believers pay the obligatory zakat; it calls payment an action because payment is itself an act.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p409#2/r5.anchor: للزكاة الواجبة مؤدون، فعبر عن التأدية بالفعل لأنها فعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p409#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p409#2/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p409#2/r6.claim: An alternate interpretation takes zakat here to mean righteous deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p409#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: الزكاة هاهنا هو العمل الصالح

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:4/r1.claim: Following bodily worship with financial worship shows they reach the utmost in religious duties and avoidance of forbidden and unbecoming things.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:4/r1.anchor: وصفهم بذلك بعد وصفهم بالخشوع في الصلاة ليدل على أنهم بلغوا الغاية في القيام على الطاعات

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:4/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:4/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:4/r2.claim: Zakāt may denote the abstract duty, since an agent performs the event rather than its object; or the material after ellipsis of a genitive noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:4/r2.anchor: والزكاة تقع على المعنى والعين والمواد الأول لأن الفاعل فاعل الحدث لا المحل الذي هو موقعه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r1.claim: Zakāt here can mean purification itself or payment of the alms that is the strongest outward proof of faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r1.anchor: أي التزكية , وهي إخراج الزكاة , أو لأداء الزكاة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r2.claim: The lām in li-l-zakāti strengthens the active participle fāʿilūn.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r2.anchor: وأثبت اللام تقوية لاسم الفاعل فقال

BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the sūra is Meccan and zakāt became obligatory in Medina in the second year after the Hijra.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r3.anchor: قال ابن كثير : هذه مكية , وإنما فرضت الزكاة بالمدينة في سنة اثنتين من الهجرة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r4.claim: The author prefers that Medina prescribed assessed zakāt on specific thresholds, while the basic obligation of zakāt already existed in Mecca.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن التي فرضت بالمدينة إنما هي ذات النصب , وأن أصل الزكاة كان واجبا بمكة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r5.claim: He supports the earlier Meccan obligation by citing 6:141, and links alms to purification in 9:103.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r5.anchor: كما قال تعالى في سورة الأنعام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p183/r6.claim: Giving wealth as due purifies, while withholding it wastes; zakāt joins purification of the heart, body, and property.

DURR-FULL:v6p87/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p87/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p87/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr interprets the zakah here as wealth.
DURR-FULL:v6p87/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {والذين هم للزكاة فاعلون} يعني: الأموال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r7.claim: Zakah here means charity, not the later fixed levy on specified wealth, so its mention does not date the sura to Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r7.anchor: فالزكاة المذكورة فيها هي الصدقة لا زكاة النصب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r8.claim: The Qur'an uses zakah for charity in Meccan Fussilat, and says Isma'il commanded his household to pray and give zakah before the fixed levy existed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p5/r8.anchor: وإطلاق الزكاة على الصدقة مشهور في القرآن ، قال تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r1.claim: Zakah originally denotes purification of the self from vices; it was extended to spending wealth for God because this purifies the donor or increases the donor's wealth, naming effect for cause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r1.anchor: أصل الزكاة أنها اسم مصدر ( زكى ) المشدد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r2.claim: Here zakah denotes the money given, using the verbal noun for its resulting object; the construction with doers requires an object, as in the command to take charity that purifies.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r2.anchor: وأطلقت على نفس المال المنفق من إطلاق اسم المصدر على المفعول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r3.claim: The object cannot be the verbal noun itself: a verb cannot take its own cognate verbal noun as object in ordinary Arabic, unlike an object or result meant by doing this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r3.anchor: وأما المصدر فلا يكون مفعولا به لفعل من مادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r4.claim: The implied action is giving zakah, equivalent to they give zakah; there is no need to supply a separate word for performance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r4.anchor: والمراد بالفعل هنا الفعل المناسب لهذا المفعول وهو الإيتاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r5.speaker: محمد بن بشير الخارجي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r5.claim: The broader word doers is chosen because this root is widely used for doing good; Muhammad ibn Bashir al-Khariji's poem illustrates spending wealth and undertaking noble acts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r5.anchor: قال محمد بن بشير الخارجي : إن تنفق المال أو تكلف مساعيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r6.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r6.claim: A poem attributed to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt uses zakah for charitable giving, but Ibn Ashur doubts its attribution because this sense may derive from Qur'anic terminology.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا الاعتبار جاء ما نسب إلى أمية بن أبي الصلت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba says scholars do not treat Umayya's poetry as authoritative evidence against the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p12/r7.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة في كتاب ( الشعر والشعراء )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r1.claim: On Ibn Ashur's reading of zakah as the object of doers, lam reinforces a weak derived verb that follows its object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r1.anchor: واللام على هذا الوجه لام التقوية لضعف العامل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم والراغب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r2.claim: Abu Muslim and al-Raghib take lam as causal, understand zakah as purification of the soul, and supply righteous deeds as the omitted object of doers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r2.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم والراغب : اللام للتعليل وجعلا الزكاة تزكية النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r3.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r3.claim: Al-Kashshaf calls zakah a verbal noun meaning the giver's act of giving zakah and says doer naturally takes such a verbal-noun complement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r3.anchor: وفي ( الكشاف ) أن الزكاة هنا مصدر وهو فعل المزكي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur says al-Kashshaf privileges formal grammar to explain the construction, and its analysis depends on an unnecessary implied noun or verbal-noun reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r4.anchor: فغلب جانب الصناعة اللفظية على جانب المعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r5.claim: Prayer and zakah frequently occur together in Qur'an; here avoiding frivolity separates them for a thematic reason discussed earlier.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r5.anchor: وعقب ذكر الصلاة بذكر الزكاة لكثرة التآخي بينهما في آيات القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r6.claim: Giving zakah is proper conduct toward people in need and belongs to ethics governing the use of wealth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r6.anchor: وهذا من آداب المعاملة مع طبقة أهل الخصاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r7.claim: The repeated relative pronoun and fronting of the object follow the same construction explained for the preceding qualities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p13/r7.anchor: والقول في إعادة الموصول وتقديم المعمول كما تقدم آنفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r12.speaker: الطبري وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r12.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and others take zakāh here to mean the obligatory alms due on wealth; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this clear.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r12.anchor: ذهب الطبري وغيره إلى أنها الزكاة المفروضة في الأموال، وهذا بين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r13.claim: The wording could also mean pursuing virtues, taking the best or purest course in every action, as in 18:81.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p136#3/r13.anchor: ويحتمل اللفظ أن يريد ب «الزكاة» الفضائل كأنه أراد الأزكى من كل فعل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p460#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p460#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p460#2/r1.claim: They perform zakat; the verse uses the general word doing because payment is an act.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p460#2/r1.anchor: للزكاة فاعلون أي مؤدون فعبر عن التأدية بالفعل لأنه فعل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r3.claim: Most commentators take zakah here as wealth alms despite the sura being Meccan; the fixed thresholds were prescribed in Medina in year two, while the basic duty likely began in Mecca, as 6:141 indicates.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r3.anchor: الأكثرون على أن المراد بالزكاة هاهنا زكاة الأموال،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r4.claim: Another possible meaning is purification of the soul from shirk and impurity, as in the verses about one who purifies the self and those who do not give zakah, on one interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r4.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون المراد بالزكاة هاهنا: زكاة النفس من الشرك والدنس، كقوله: {قد أفلح من زكاها. وقد خاب من دساها}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r5.claim: Both meanings may be intended: purification of souls and almsgiving from wealth; the complete believer practices both.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p462/r5.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون كلا الأمرين مرادا، وهو زكاة النفوس وزكاة الأموال؛ فإنه من جملة زكاة النفوس،

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.claim: The listed traits remove ambiguity: whoever has them is a believer, supporting the author’s position.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r5.anchor: ثم بين تعالى ما أزال كل شبهة، فذكر صفات المؤمن، فدل أن من كانت صفته ما ذكر

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r11.claim: Zakat is obligatory and a condition of faith, subject to conditions such as ownership of the minimum amount for a full year.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r11.anchor: وتدل على وجوب الزكاة، وأنها من شرائط الإيمان، وذلك لا يجب إلا بشرائط ملك النصاب

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r12.claim: Zakat is a legally prescribed act of worship.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r12.anchor: وتدل على أن الزكاة عبادة شرعية

JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.claim: No other required duties are omitted: worship, contracts, and liabilities fall under trusts and covenants; sins fall under avoiding laghw.
JISHUMI:v7p5024/r18.anchor: قلنا: لا؛ لأن جميع ما كلف دخل في الآية؛ لأن جميع ما يجب فعله من العبادات

MUQATIL:23:1-6/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:1-6/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:1-6/r4.claim: Doing zakah means paying the zakah due on their wealth.
MUQATIL:23:1-6/r4.anchor: { والذين هم للزكاة فاعلون } [آية: 4] يعنى زكاة أموالهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r1.claim: They perform zakat, and the wording “doers” suggests continuing practice more clearly than “payers.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r1.anchor: مؤدون وبفظ فاعلون يدل على المداومة بخلاف مؤدون

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r2.claim: Zakat can mean the payment itself or the act of purification; the latter is intended, with the performers named for doing it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r2.anchor: وقيل الزكاة اسم مشترك يطلق على العين وهو القدر الذى يخرجه المزكى من النصاب إلى الفقير وعلى المعنى وهو فعل المزكى الذى هو التزكية وهو المراد هنا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r3.claim: Alternatively, zakat means the payment, with “performance” omitted; the preceding object takes a lām because the active participle has weaker verbal force.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p116#5/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالزكاة العين ويقدر مضاف محذوف وهو الاداء ودخل اللام لتقدم المفعول وضعف اسم الفاعل

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r13.claim: The author says the meanings of idle talk and zakat were already discussed in al-Baqara and need not be repeated.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r13.anchor: وتقدم في «البقرة» معنى اللغو والزكاة فلا معنى للإعادة

QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r17.claim: Fāʿilūn means those who perform or pay it; this usage is eloquent and attested in Arab speech, including poetry by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:4/r17.anchor: ومعنى «فاعلون» أي مؤدون وهي فصيحة، وقد جاءت في كلام العرب

QASHANI:23:1-11/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:23:1-11/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:23:1-11/r4.claim: Their zakat is detachment from their own traits.
QASHANI:23:1-11/r4.anchor: { والذين هم للزكاة فاعلون } بالتجرد عن صفاتهم

STUDYQURAN:23:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:4/r1.claim: Zakāh can mean charity generally, but in Islamic usage became the required yearly alms from accumulated liquid wealth.
STUDYQURAN:23:4/r1.anchor: term came to denote the required yearly alms paid from accumulated liquid

QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r11.claim: Zakat means growth, but spiritual growth requires diminishing one’s own self-witness; complete servitude comes only by dissolving that witness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p335/r11.anchor: الزكاة النماء ، ومن عمله للنماء فأمارة ذلك أن يكون بنقصانه في نفسه عن شواهده

TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.claim: The traits in the opening passage show faith as living and active, producing its effects so that the believer reaches the intended end, success.
TABATABAI:23:1-11/r1.anchor: وهذه الآية إلى تمام ثماني آيات تذكر من أوصاف المؤمنين ما يلازم كون وصف الإيمان حيا فعالا

TABATABAI:23:4-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r1.claim: Because zakah is paired with prayer in a Meccan surah, it means financial giving or purifying wealth through expenditure, not the later fixed alms amount or cleansing the soul of vices.
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r1.anchor: ذكر الزكاة مع الصلاة قرينة على كون المراد بها الإنفاق المالي دون الزكاة بمعنى تطهير النفس بإزالة رذائل الأخلاق

TABATABAI:23:4-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r2.speaker: بعض من حمل الزكاة على هذا المعنى
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r2.claim: Some who take zakah as the fixed amount supply an implied word meaning its payment, yielding 'performers of zakah payment.'
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r2.anchor: ولذا قدر بعض من حمل الزكاة على هذا المعنى لفظ التأدية فكان التقدير عنده

TABATABAI:23:4-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r3.claim: Some interpret zakah as purification of the soul from reprehensible traits to avoid attaching 'for zakah' directly to 'doers.'
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r3.anchor: ولذا أيضا فسر بعضهم الزكاة بتطهير النفس عن الأخلاق الرذيلة فرارا من تعلق

TABATABAI:23:4-7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r4.claim: Taking zakah as an act of spending makes its attachment to 'doers' natural; treating it as the extracted money does not, since money is not an action performed by an agent.
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r4.anchor: وأما لو كان المراد بالزكاة نفس المال المخرج لم يصح تعلقه به إذ المال المخرج ليس فعلا متعلقا بفاعل

TABATABAI:23:4-7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r5.claim: Saying they are active doers of zakah, rather than merely payers, stresses their care for it, like saying 'I will do it' when asked to drink water.
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r5.anchor: دون أن يقول للزكاة مؤدون أو ما يؤدي معناه دلالة على عنايتهم بها

TABATABAI:23:4-7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r6.claim: Faith should prompt giving because happiness requires a community where people receive their rights and enjoy life's benefits more equally; aid to poor people is a strong means toward it.
TABATABAI:23:4-7/r6.anchor: ومن حق الإيمان بالله أن يدعو إلى هذا الإنفاق المالي فإن الإنسان لا ينال كمال سعادته إلا في مجتمع سعيد

TABATABAI:23:1-11#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:1-11#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:1-11#6/r6.claim: Social customs and laws answer recognized human needs; basic needs close to nature demand priority, and neglecting them causes greater harm than neglecting luxuries.
TABATABAI:23:1-11#6/r6.anchor: الذي يدعو الإنسان ويبعثه نحو الاستنان بالسنن الاجتماعية أو وضع القوانين الجارية في المجتمع البشري

TABRISI:23:4-10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:4-10/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:4-10/r1.claim: The phrase means they pay alms; payment is called doing because it is an act, with Umayya’s line cited as evidence.
TABRISI:23:4-10/r1.anchor: أي مؤدون فعبر عن التأدية بالفعل لأنه فعل قال أمية بن أبي الصلت

TABRISI:23:4-10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:4-10/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:23:4-10/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas specifies that they perform the obligatory alms.
TABRISI:23:4-10/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس للصدقة الواجبة مؤدون

THALABI:v7p39/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p39/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p39/r6.claim: The believers perform and pay the obligatory zakat.
THALABI:v7p39/r6.anchor: والذين هم للزكاة الواجبة فاعلون مؤدون، وهي فصيحة

THALABI:v7p39/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p39/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p39/r7.claim: The expression is good Arabic usage; Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt’s verse likewise speaks of paying zakat.
THALABI:v7p39/r7.anchor: المطعمون الطعام في السنة … الأزمة والفاعلون للزكوات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says they give zakat from their wealth seeking God’s pleasure.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يزكون أموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says they fulfill the obligatory charity.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p523/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq explains فاعلون as مؤتون, “giving.”

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:1-7/r4.claim: Being active in zakat means paying the obligatory alms.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p393/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p393/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p393/r3.claim: They perform the obligatory alms payment.

ELMALILI:23:3-8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r2.claim: The immediate sense of doing zakat is giving zakat from one's wealth.
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r2.anchor: bundan mütebâdir olan mâna, mallarının zekâtını verirler demektir.

ELMALILI:23:3-8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r3.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r3.claim: Some understand zakat here to mean refinement and purification.
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r3.anchor: bazıları bu ifadeye nazaran “zekât”tan murad, tehzib ve tahâret mânası olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:23:3-8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r4.claim: Elmalılı says “doing the work of zakat” can include purification of the self, body, and wealth.
ELMALILI:23:3-8/r4.anchor: “Zekât işini yaparlar” demek nefsî, bedenî, mâlî zekâtın hepsine de şâmil olabilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r1.claim: Because obligatory zakat was prescribed in Medina after this Meccan sūra, zakat here must be used broadly for charity (ṣadaqa).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r1.anchor: buradaki zekât kelimesi geniş anlamıyla sadaka yerine kullanılmış olmalıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r2.claim: The Qur’an sometimes uses zakat and ṣadaqa interchangeably; 9:60 calls the recipients’ obligatory zakat ṣadaqa.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r2.anchor: farz olan zekâtın kimlere verileceğini açıklayan âyette de zekât yerine sadaka kelimesi kullanılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r3.claim: Although obligatory zakat came later, Meccan revelations already strongly encouraged financial aid through ṣadaqa, zakat, spending, beneficence, and feeding.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:4/r3.anchor: Mekke döneminde inen âyetlerde de sadaka, zekât, infak, ihsan, it‘âm gibi kelimelerle müslümanlar malî yardımlaşmaya teşvik edilmekte

NAHHAS:v3p109/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p109/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p109/r6.claim: God praises even those who give only the zakāt due from their wealth; hoarders of gold and silver are those who fail to pay zakāt.
NAHHAS:v3p109/r6.anchor: فمدح الله جل وعز ومن أخرج من ماله الزكاة وإن لم يخرج منه غيرها فكأن الذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة هم الذين لا يخرجون الزكاة

BURHAN:v4p83/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p83/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p83/r2.claim: عملوا الصالحات suggests persistence in good works; افعلوا الخير means hasten to do good, as reinforced by فاستبقوا الخيرات and by prompt payment to meet the poor’s needs.
BURHAN:v4p83/r2.anchor: حيث كان المقصود المثابرة عليها لا الإتيان بها مرة

ITQAN:v2p570/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p570/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p570/r6.claim: ʿAmila usually marks an action extended over time, while faʿala marks quick action; hence sustained good works use the former and prompt action the latter.
ITQAN:v2p570/r6.anchor: فالأول لما كان من امتداد زمان نحو ﴿ يعملون له ما يشاء ﴾

KHATTABI:v1p37/r7.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p37/r7.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p37/r7.claim: An objection says that Arabic does not say someone ‘does zakāh’; it uses verbs such as give, pay, or purify one’s wealth.
KHATTABI:v1p37/r7.anchor: ولا يقول أحد من الناس: فعل زيد الزكاة , إنما يقال: زكى الرجل ماله

KHATTABI:v1p44/r7.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p44/r7.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p44/r7.claim: ‘Doers of zakāh’ conveys sustained, habitual performance as a defining trait, whereas ordinary verbs merely report that payment occurred; this is the most complete and forceful wording.
KHATTABI:v1p44/r7.anchor: ومعنى الكلام ومراده المبالغة في أدائها والمواظبة عليه حتى يكون ذلك صفة لازمة لهم

KHATTABI:v1p44/r8.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p44/r8.speaker: قيل
KHATTABI:v1p44/r8.claim: Another view takes zakāh here as righteous work and virtuous deeds, so the phrase means that they perform good and pure actions.
KHATTABI:v1p44/r8.anchor: وقد قيل إن معنى الزكاة هنا العمل الصالح الزاكي

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.claim: Umar describes revelation’s bee-like sound and the Prophet’s supplication, then reports that whoever upholds the first ten verses of al-Muʾminun enters Paradise.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p312/r1.anchor: سمعت عمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنه - يقول

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r1.claim: Zakat can mean the act of purification or giving alms, so فاعلون means they perform the act, like someone who performs striking or killing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r1.anchor: ويصح أن تكون (الزكاة) بمعنى التزكية وهو الحدث، أي: فِعْل المزكّي، فيكون (فاعلون) بمعناها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r2.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r2.claim: Al-Kashshaf distinguishes the alms amount from the act of purification and says the latter is intended; it also allows the amount with an implied word for its payment.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r2.anchor: جاء في (الكشاف) : "الزكاة اسم مشترك بين عين ومعنى. فالعين القدْر الذي يُخرجه المزكّي من النصاب إلى الفقير.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r3.speaker: البحر المحيط
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r3.claim: Al-Bahr al-Muhit says فاعلون fits purification as an action; if zakat means the alms amount, the phrase implies أداء الزكاة or takes فاعلون to mean those who pay it, as al-Tabrizi explains.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p139/r3.anchor: وجاء في (البحر المحيط) : "والزكاة إن أريد بها التزكية صَحَّ نِسبةُ الفعل إليها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r1.claim: Zakat may mean purification of the soul from idolatry and impurity, alms from wealth, or both; the complete believer performs both forms of purification.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r1.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون المراد بالزكاة ههنا زكاةُ النفس من الشرك والدنس كقوله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r2.claim: Zakat is brought forward for emphasis, care, and restriction: they perform only good, including zakat.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r2.anchor: وتقديم الزكاة للاهتمام والعناية والقصر، أي: لا يفعلون إلا الخير، والزكاة منها.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r3.claim: Unlike zakat, whose required payment completes the duty, prayer's outward motions need humility, reflection, presence of heart, and proper manners to complete it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r3.anchor: والجواب: أن إخراج النصاب إلى مستحقه كافٍ لأداء فريضة الزكاة، وليس وراءه شيء يتعلق بها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r4.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying that a person receives from prayer only what they consciously understand.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p142/r4.anchor: ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لكَ من صلاتك ما عقلتَ منها"، فاتضح الفرق بينهما.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.claim: The commands to bow, prostrate, worship, do good, establish prayer and give zakat match the opening of al-Muʾminun and its listed believer qualities.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r1.anchor: فأنت ترى من الأمر بالركوع والسجود وعبادة الله، وفعل الخير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r4.claim: Imperative acts such as bowing, prostration, prayer and zakat become stable believer traits, expressed through nominal descriptions of humility, turning from idle talk and giving zakat.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p128/r4.anchor: فاتصفوا بما أمرهم به ربهم على وجه الثبات، فوصفهم بالصيغة الاسمية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r1.claim: In المؤمنون 23:4, الزكاة can mean the amount of wealth paid to its rightful recipient.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r1.anchor: فإن (الزكاة) اسم مشترك بين عدة معانٍ، فقد يطلق على القَدْر الذي يخرجه المزكّي من ماله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r2.claim: الزكاة can also be the verbal noun تزكية: the act of paying the prescribed amount from one's wealth to its recipient.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r2.anchor: وقد يطلق على المصدر بمعنى: التزكية، وهو الحدث، والمعنى: إخراج القدْر المفروض من الأموال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r3.claim: الزكاة can mean righteous action and purification of the self from idolatry and defilement, as the cited verses use it for purity and purification.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r3.anchor: وقد تكون بمعنى العمل الصالح، وتطهير النفس من الشرك والدنس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r4.claim: The financial, verbal, righteous-action and purification senses can all be intended together in this compact expression.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r4.anchor: وهذه المعاني مجتمعة يصح أن تكون مرادة في هذا التعبير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r5.claim: The verse can mean that believers pay zakat by construing فاعلون as مؤدون or estimating a deleted noun, لأداء الزكاة.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r5.anchor: وذلك على تضمين (فاعلون) معنى (مؤدّون) أو على تقدير مضاف محذوف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r6.claim: On another parse, الزكاة is the object of فاعلون, fronted for exclusivity; the lām reinforces the relation and is called لام التقوية, as in 2:91.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r6.anchor: فالزكاة مفعولٌ به لاسم الفاعل (فاعلون) ، ثم قدم المفعول للاختصاص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r7.claim: With either grammatical analysis, الزكاة denotes the concrete wealth paid to its rightful recipient.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p138/r7.anchor: وبهذين التقديرين يكون المقصود بالزكاة اسم العين، وهو المال الذي يخرج لمستحقه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r1.claim: Abu Muslim reads الزكاة here as righteous work, as in the cited description خيراً منه زكاة; al-Bahr also reports this view.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r1.anchor: وعن أبي مسلم أن الزكاة هنا بمعنى العمل الصالح كما في قوله تعالى: {خَيْراً مِّنْهُ زَكَاةً}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r2.speaker: الراغب
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r2.claim: Al-Raghib takes الزكاة to mean purity and the lām as causal: they worship so God purifies them or they purify themselves.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r2.anchor: واختار الراغب أن الزكاة بمعنى الطهارة، واللام للتعليل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r3.claim: Al-Kashshaf says they do good for the sake of purity and self-purification, supported by the verses about purification and prayer.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r3.anchor: قال صاحب "الكشاف"، معنى الآية، الذين هم لأجل الطهارة وتزكية النفس عاملون الخير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r4.claim: Another view in al-Bahr reads الزكاة as growth and increase, with a causal lām and an omitted object: doing good to attain growth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r4.anchor: وقيل: الزكاة هنا: النماء والزيادة. واللام لام العلة ومعمول فاعلون محذوف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r5.claim: The verse can intend financial zakat, righteous work, purification and growth together; its lām can strengthen the construction or express purpose.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r5.anchor: فالزكاة إذن تحتمل العبادة المالية، وتحتمل العمل الصالح والتطهير والنماء، واللام تحتمل التقوية، وتحتمل التعليل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r6.claim: Replacing فاعلون with مؤتون would restrict the meaning to financial zakat, while removing the lām would lose the purpose sense; no other wording gathers all the meanings so simply.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r6.anchor: فلو أبدل كلمة (مؤتون) مكان (فاعلون) لاقتصر الأمر على زكاة المال، ولو حذف اللام لم يفد معنى التعليل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r7.speaker: ابن كثير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir reports that most interpreters take this as financial zakat despite the verse being Meccan; the zakat instituted in Medina in year two appears to be the threshold-based obligation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p141/r7.anchor: جاء في (تفسير ابن كثير) : "الأكثرون على أن المراد بالزكاة ههنا زكاة الأموال

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r5.claim: Zakāh is faith's second manifestation and prayer's second arm; together they are religion's two primary directives and the basis of all sharīʿah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r5.anchor: These are the two premier directives of religion and all the sharī‘ah is based on these two.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r6.claim: Islahi says Abū Bakr's campaign against those withholding zakāh followed from the principle that rejecting either primary directive undermines adherence to both.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r6.anchor: The attack launched by Abū Bakr (rta) against those who were desisting to pay zakāh was based on this philosophy of religion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.claim: The next sūrah, al-Nūr, supplements this one: faith illuminating the inner self brightens individual and collective life, while its absence darkens both.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r11.anchor: Details of all these points will be found in the next sūrah: Sūrah al-Nūr which is the supplement of this sūrah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.claim: Islahi summarizes the earlier passage as a progression from inward faith through prayer, zakāh, restraint, fidelity, and guarded prayer to lasting success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p243/r13.anchor: on them depends the success of the believers.
